key_insight: A backward-mapping, genome-guided pipeline can translate device targets into chemically interpretable rules to discover stable, lead-free double perovskites.
engineering_relevance: The framework narrows a 13,088-composition search space to seven DFT-validated candidates, offering a scalable route for inverse design of safer photovoltaic materials.
method: Filtered charge-balanced A2BB'X6 compositions with halide-aware geometric formability rules.
Encoded six families of chemical-genome descriptors and trained evolutionary-optimized ML surrogates for stability and band gap.
Used SHAP interpretation plus DFT closure to validate phase stability, electronic structure, and optical properties.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports screening 13,088 compositions and validating seven candidates with DFT, including stability, band-edge character, effective masses, dielectric response, absorption, reflectivity, and XRD fingerprints.
watch_item: The workflow relies on surrogate models and PBE-based band gaps, so final material performance still depends on DFT accuracy and experimental synthesis validation.
paper_title: Backward Mapping from Device Targets to Chemical Genomes for Interpretable Discovery of Phase-Stable Lead-Free Double Perovskites with DFT-Validated Design Rules
